science_review: Cartesian central springs at finite stiffness, followed by equilibration and the ordered stiffness limits, give the independent solid-angle measure. The scalar x clamp with transverse coordinates free measures the log derivative of a projected endpoint density. Inverting a force-controlled mean response is a well-defined but different finite-chain statistical experiment. The exact polynomial derivative, Fourier reference and finite-clamp mechanical force have consistent signs and normalization.
identification_review: Every positive-force calibration setting is strictly increasing in the unknown link length. The analytic derivative and independent angular integration establish identification without any hidden clamp data.
public_input_review: Keep potentials, known temperatures/forces, unknown length bounds, transverse freedom, signed force, and limit order. Remove the interpretive constrained-Hamiltonian contrast, fix b as unknown and specify X/N in fixed L0 units. No convolution, derivative or correction formula and no solver mandate belong in the public instruction. These refinements are saved separately while the original outline remains preserved.
limitations: No task package or model difficulty has yet been evaluated.
The 5.24% minimum is a sampled corner gap; full parameter, all integer N, and 256-noise checks remain required.
A trial that recognizes the correct ensemble but miscoded the polynomial or derivative is not a clean physical-model failure.
